questions.question: Dr. Chamssi received a suspicious email with an attachment. Dr. Tazi advises him not to open it. What is the main threat of phishing emails in a dental practice?
options: Theft of personal data and installation of malware
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Phishing aims to steal credentials and install malware that can encrypt your data.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will train my team to recognize these emails.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses the same password for all his software. Dr. Tazi recommends changing this practice. What is the fundamental rule of passwords in a dental practice?
options: Use the same password everywhere to avoid forgetting
Use unique, complex passwords and change them regularly
Write passwords on a Post-it stuck to the screen
Use simple passwords for less important software
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Unique and complex passwords limit the impact of a data leak.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will use a password manager.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi was a victim of ransomware. Dr. Tazi helps him manage the crisis. What is the first thing to do in the event of a ransomware attack?
options: Isolate the infected machine from the network and contact a cybersecurity expert
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Isolating the infected machine prevents the ransomware from spreading to other machines in the practice.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will cut the network immediately.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi lost all his data due to ransomware. Dr. Tazi kept his paper files. What is Dr. Chamssi missing to avoid this situation?
options: A backup plan (BCP) with offline copies
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'A regular backup plan with offline copies allows restoring data without paying the ransom.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will set up automated backups.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi must notify a security incident. Dr. Tazi asks him about his obligations. According to the CNDP, what is the maximum deadline for notifying a personal data breach?
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The CNDP recommends notifying the breach within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will prepare an urgent notification procedure.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi installed management software without checking its security updates. Dr. Tazi reminds him of the importance of updates. Why are updates crucial?
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Updates fix vulnerabilities that could be exploited by cyber attackers.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will enable automatic updates.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized his files and makes them remotely accessible via a VPN. Dr. Tazi still uses paper files. According to the CNDP, must Dr. Chamssi secure his VPN?
options: No, the VPN is secure by default
Yes, the VPN must be configured with secure protocols and strong authentication
Yes, but only if the patient requests it
No, because the data is already encrypted
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'A poorly configured VPN can expose data. You must use secure protocols like OpenVPN or WireGuard.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will check my VPN configuration.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi and Dr. Tazi compare the European GDPR and Moroccan Law 09-08. What is the main difference regarding financial sanctions?
options: The GDPR provides for fines up to 20 million euros, Law 09-08 up to 100,000 DH
Law 09-08 is stricter than the GDPR
Both provide for the same amounts
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'The GDPR is more severe in terms of financial sanctions, but Law 09-08 imposes similar obligations.' Dr. Tazi: 'We must respect both if we process European data.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses teleradiology software to exchange images with a colleague. Dr. Tazi uses mail. According to the CNDP, what obligation applies to Dr. Chamssi?
options: Encrypt exchanges and obtain patient consent
Make an additional declaration to the ministry
Use software certified by the Order
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Exchanges of health data must be encrypted and the patient must be informed.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will secure my radiology exchanges.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has installed video surveillance cameras. Dr. Tazi has a mirror without a camera. According to the CNDP, where must Dr. Chamssi inform patients of the presence of cameras?
options: At the entrance of the practice and in the filmed area
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Information must be visible at the entrance and in the filmed area so that patients are informed.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will install information signs.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi wishes to use artificial intelligence to analyze X-rays. Dr. Tazi questions the compliance. According to the CNDP, must Dr. Chamssi obtain prior authorization?
options: Yes, because AI involves automated processing of health data
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'AI analyzing health data is considered automated processing requiring prior authorization.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will make an authorization request.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has subscribed to a cloud storage service for his backups. Dr. Tazi keeps his backups locally. According to Law 09-08, must Dr. Chamssi inform his patients of the location where their data is stored?
options: No, the storage location does not matter
Yes, the patient must be informed of the country where their data is stored
Yes, but only if the storage is outside Morocco
No, because the cloud is always secure
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The patient must be informed if their data is transferred outside Morocco, because it involves different protection.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will inform my patients of the storage location.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has digitized his files with a scanner. Dr. Tazi still photocopies his documents. Regarding data retention, what is the common obligation for both?
options: Guarantee the integrity and confidentiality of data, regardless of the medium
Keep documents only in paper format
questions.explanation: Dr. Chamssi explains: 'Regardless of the medium, we have the obligation to guarantee the integrity and confidentiality of data.' Dr. Tazi: 'I will secure my paper archives.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi uses online appointment management software. Dr. Tazi uses a paper diary. According to the CNDP, must Dr. Chamssi declare this software?
options: No, appointments are not personal data
Yes, because it collects personal data (name, phone, email)
Yes, but only if the software is paid
No, if the software is hosted in Morocco
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Collecting personal data via online appointment software must be declared to the CNDP.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will make the declaration for my software.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi was a victim of a data leak following a hack. Dr. Tazi advises him on the procedure. What should Dr. Chamssi do first?
options: Secure the system to stop the leak
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The first priority is to stop the leak by securing the system, then inform the CNDP and patients.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will first isolate the infected system.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi installed an antivirus but did not activate the firewall. Dr. Tazi explains his mistake. What is the function of a firewall in a dental practice?
options: Block unauthorized access to the practice's network
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The firewall acts as a barrier that filters access to the practice's network.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will activate my firewall.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi received a request for access to his data from a patient. Dr. Tazi reminds him of the procedure. According to Law 09-08, within what period must Dr. Chamssi respond to this request?
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The legal deadline for responding to a request for access to personal data is 1 month.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will prepare the documents to respond to the patient.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi responded to a patient's access request. Dr. Tazi asks him if he has properly justified his response. What must the response to an access request contain?
options: The requested data and a copy of the consents
The requested data, information on rights, and the complaint form
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The response must include the data, information on rights, and the complaint procedure.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will prepare a complete response.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi was contacted by a patient who wishes to rectify their personal data. Dr. Tazi explains the procedure. According to Law 09-08, what is the patient's right?
options: The patient can request the rectification of inaccurate data
The patient cannot rectify their medical data
The patient must go through a lawyer
Rectification requires the consent of the CNDP
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The right of rectification allows the patient to have inaccurate data corrected.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will correct the patient's data.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi received a formal notice from the CNDP concerning a breach. Dr. Tazi helps him understand the stakes. What does Dr. Chamssi risk in the event of persistent non-compliance?
options: A fine of 10,000 to 100,000 DH and/or criminal sanctions
The definitive closure of the practice
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The CNDP can impose fines of 10,000 to 100,000 DH and initiate criminal proceedings.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will regularize my situation immediately.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi has outsourced the hosting of his data to a provider. Dr. Tazi warns him of his responsibilities. According to Law 09-08, must Dr. Chamssi control his provider?
options: No, the provider is solely responsible
Yes, Dr. Chamssi remains responsible for the processing and must control his subcontractor
Yes, but only if the provider is foreign
No, the law does not provide for this obligation
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The data controller remains fully responsible for data protection, even when outsourced.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will audit my provider.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi lost his laptop containing unencrypted patient data. Dr. Tazi informs him of the consequences. What is Dr. Chamssi's first obligation?
options: Notify the loss to the CNDP and the patients concerned
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The loss of a device containing unencrypted data constitutes a data breach requiring notification.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will notify the CNDP and the patients.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi decided to use passwords for his software. Dr. Tazi recommends using two-factor authentication (2FA). What is the advantage of 2FA?
options: A double layer of security: password + temporary code
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: '2FA adds an extra layer of security beyond the password, making credential theft more difficult.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will enable 2FA on all my software.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi was confronted with a security incident. Dr. Tazi recommends keeping an incident register. Why is this register important?
options: It is a legal obligation without practical interest
It allows tracking incidents for the CNDP and improving security
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'The incident register allows tracking security events and proving compliance during an audit.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will create an incident register.'

questions.question: Dr. Chamssi, after securing his IT system with Dr. Tazi, receives his congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Chamssi?
options: Become an expert in dental cybersecurity
questions.explanation: Dr. Tazi explains: 'Mastery of cybersecurity is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Chamssi: 'I will train in cybersecurity.'
